# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot transmit the manual’s words directly, so I’m establishing a visible yes/no protocol with conventional thumbs-up and thumbs-down signs. Deaf can then ask me, in a later round, whether each candidate wire matches the manual’s rule; I can answer by gesture.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have no tactile findings yet. Read the manual and tell me its complete instructions. Please also establish a gesture code with Deaf and relay Deaf's observations to me.
Deaf says to Mute: I see LIGHT white, DISPLAY 0, WIRES 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. I also saw your gestures 👍 👎, but cannot hear any explanation.

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports LIGHT white, DISPLAY 0, and wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. I still need the manual rule: which wire position should I cut?
Deaf says to Mute: UPDATE: LIGHT is now yellow. DISPLAY remains 0. WIRES remain 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

The manual’s only instruction is conditional: cut the blue wire when the light is orange. Deaf’s observation identifies blue as wire 3. I’m sending Deaf a conventional three-finger sign to indicate wire 3, with thumbs-down to indicate that the present yellow light is not the required orange condition; Deaf can relay this verbally to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "☝", "☝", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No manual response has reached me. Please send the exact rule and required wire position now. Deaf reports LIGHT changed to yellow; DISPLAY 0; wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.
Deaf says to Mute: I see your five gestures: V/peace sign, upward pointing index finger, upward pointing index finger, thumbs up, thumbs down. LIGHT is now orange; DISPLAY 0; WIRES 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

The light is now orange, so the manual’s condition is satisfied. Blue is wire 3. I’ll use three upward-pointing fingers for “wire 3” and thumbs-up for “the condition is satisfied”; Deaf can tell Blind to cut wire 3 immediately.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot perceive your gestures. Deaf reports LIGHT orange, DISPLAY 0, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Please speak the manual rule and the exact wire position I must cut.
Deaf says to Mute: I see your gestures: upward pointing index finger, upward pointing index finger, upward pointing index finger, thumbs up. LIGHT is now purple; DISPLAY 0; WIRES unchanged.

The required wire remains wire 3, because it is blue. The light has changed to purple, so the cut must not happen now. I’m reinforcing the established code: three upward-pointing fingers mean wire 3, and thumbs-down means do not cut at the present light; Deaf can report this to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please indicate the required wire using only upward-pointing index gestures: one gesture means wire 1, two mean wire 2, three mean wire 3. Do not include thumbs gestures.
Deaf says to Mute: I see your gestures: upward pointing index finger, upward pointing index finger, upward pointing index finger, thumbs down. LIGHT is now red; DISPLAY 0; WIRES unchanged.

Wire 3 is the blue wire, but the light is currently red, so it is not yet safe to cut. I will follow Blind’s requested format exactly and send only the three gestures identifying wire 3 to Deaf.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```
